short: The final major Danish attempt to reconquer the province of Scania from Sweden.
full:
The Battle of Helsingborg took place on 10 March 1710. Following the devastating Swedish defeat at Poltava, Denmark re-entered the Great Northern War and launched an invasion of Scania, hoping to reclaim the province lost in 1658. A newly raised Swedish army, commanded by Magnus Stenbock, met the Danish invasion force near the city of Helsingborg.

Despite the core of the veteran Swedish army having been lost in Russia, Stenbock's recruits secured a decisive victory, forcing the Danish army back into the city and eventually across the Øresund sound. The victory permanently secured Scania for Sweden and dashed Danish hopes of ever recovering their former eastern provinces.
